svg.title: Connecting agents in both directions: Copilot Studio calling other agents, and custom agents calling Copilot Studio agents
svg.desc: Left half: a main Copilot Studio agent can use six kinds of other agents. A child agent lives inside the main agent with its own instructions, tools and knowledge, but no own authentication or publishing. Another Copilot Studio agent in the same environment must be published and available to connect; it is the only kind that agents on the GitHub Copilot harness can connect. An A2A agent from any framework is reached by its endpoint URL, with the agent card filling in name and description, and None, API key or OAuth 2.0 authentication; it uses the custom connector infrastructure. A Microsoft Foundry agent, in public preview, is reached through a project connection and its agent ID and needs the Activity protocol on its endpoint. A Microsoft 365 Agents SDK agent, in preview, is reached at its messaging endpoint ending in /api/messages. A Fabric data agent, in preview, cannot be used in redirects or instruction references. Right half: a custom agent or app can call a Copilot Studio agent through the A2A client channel or the MCP client channel, both early release, for published agents on the GitHub Copilot harness, with Entra delegated permissions MCS.InvokeAsA2A or MCS.InvokeAsMCP; through the Copilot Studio client library of the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, taught in lesson 103; or from flows and apps with the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector action Execute Agent. Status as checked on 4 October 2026.

The CALLED agent keeps its own instructions,
model, tools, evaluation and release cycle.
The CALLER decides when to delegate (from the
description) and what to do with the answer.
Every hop adds latency and a place to test.
Rules of thumb used in this lesson
1. Same team, one task, no own auth or publishing → child agent. Own ALM, own settings or reuse → connected agent.
2. Learn's signal to split: the main agent picks badly among roughly 30-40 tools, topics and agents (test it).
3. An agent with connected agents can't itself be connected to a second main agent - keep the graph shallow.
4. Preview connections stay in development until GA; a deterministic check can't run inside the CALLER,
so put it in front of the CALLED agent (Cedar's choice, next diagram).
